This is so different than the experiences I’ve had before, and she’s not a tech who I recognize. Needless to say; this was a terrible experience and so close to my wedding.. I’m a bit nervous for my wedding set next week… so I cancelled my next fill.

I had an extremely frustrating experience with Purolator and will not use their service again.

First, my shipment could not be delivered because the address was incorrect. I contacted Purolator, corrected the address, and was told by a representative that it would take about one business day to update and sort everything. After that, I was told the package would be delivered to the corrected address, but it took another four business days to be delivered.

When the package was finally marked as delivered, Purolator delivered it to the WRONG ADDRESS again. I contacted them because I could not find my package, and I was initially told that it had been delivered to the correct address. I was also told that the sender had not requested a signature, which made it feel as though the responsibility was being pushed back on me.

I had to call again and ask for proof of delivery. Once I was finally able to see the delivery photo, it clearly showed that the package had been left at the wrong address. I then had to go around looking for my own package because of their delivery mistake.

What made this experience especially disappointing was not just the incorrect delivery, but the way my concern was handled. Instead of properly investigating when I first reported that the package was missing, I was told it had been delivered correctly.

This was one of the worst delivery experiences I have had. After correcting the address directly with Purolator, I expected the package to actually be delivered to that address. I will not be using Purolator again.

one_star_reviews.text:
********UPDATE *********

I have preserved every communication and piece of documentation related to this matter, including the communications that have occurred since I posted this review, and I fully intend to follow through with the appropriate channels to ensure my concerns are properly addressed.
I also have evidence that my next counselling appointment was booked for August 11, 2026. I had resumed counselling with Limitless Wellness in March 2026, my last session was June 2, and I had another appointment scheduled for August. This documentation is particularly important considering the practice's public response suggesting that I was not identified as an active client with a future appointment.
Instead of acknowledging this discrepancy, the public response to my review has continued to be edited and expanded. I have not been engaging with the owner throughout this. I have simply been documenting what has occurred.
What I find deeply concerning is that this is a counselling practice. Conflict resolution, communication, compassion and emotional safety should matter. Yet when I raised a legitimate concern about unexpectedly losing access to my counsellor and continuity of care, I did not experience those qualities.
Instead, I received an email addressing my review, followed by a formal legal demand requesting its removal, and I have now watched the public response to my review repeatedly change while responsibility continues to be placed elsewhere.
At no point was I offered an actual solution to the problem that started all of this: I unexpectedly lost my counsellor despite having a future appointment booked.
This stopped being only about the original incident for me. The way my complaint has subsequently been handled has become equally concerning.
I have the documentation to support the factual statements I am making, including evidence of my August 11 appointment. The appropriate professional channels will receive the relevant documentation and communications so that they can independently determine whether professional standards were met.
I also intend to speak publicly about my own experience and the importance of accountability and continuity of care in counselling services. Consumers have a right to discuss their experiences with businesses, and I will continue to do so truthfully and based on the documentation I have retained.
I will not engage in an ongoing public argument. I have said what happened to me, I have preserved my evidence, and I will allow the appropriate process to address the rest.
I do not wish to receive further direct communication from this practice regarding my review.

************************

I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel compelled to share my experience.

I had been seeing my therapist through Limitless Wellness since 2023 and had built a strong therapeutic relationship over several years. Recently, I discovered that my therapist was no longer with the clinic—but not because the clinic informed me.

I never received a phone call, email, or any other notification that my therapist had left or that my appointments had been cancelled. The only reason I found out was because I reached out to my therapist myself to ask whether we had another appointment booked. If I hadn't contacted her, I honestly don't know when or how I would have found out.

My issue is not that therapists move on to other opportunities. That happens, and I completely respect that. My concern is how clients were handled during this transition. Ending a long-term therapeutic relationship without notifying the client, providing guidance, or offering any closure is incredibly disappointing.

Mental health care is built on trust and continuity. Clients invest years building a relationship with their therapist, and they deserve to be treated with respect and kept informed when significant changes affect their care.

Based on my experience, the lack of communication from the clinic was unacceptable, and I hope they improve their processes so future clients are not left in the same position.

one_star_reviews.text:
I contacted NB ACORN at the beginning of August because I was dealing with serious concerns about the living conditions in my apartment complex and was looking for support.

During my initial conversation, I was given very high expectations about what NB ACORN would do to help. I was told, essentially, that they would organize a large group response, go door-to-door throughout the complex to speak with other tenants about their concerns, gather information, look into the situation, and involve the media if appropriate. I was also told that they would be coming to the complex the following week.

I was very encouraged by this conversation. I thought I had finally found an organization that was prepared to stand with tenants and actually take action.

I was then told that membership would cost $30 per month. Given everything I had been told they were going to do, I considered that a reasonable amount and agreed to become a member.

Unfortunately, that is not what happened.
The promised visit never happened. Nobody came to the complex the following Wednesday, and despite multiple follow-ups from me, the situation continued without the assistance I had been promised. I repeatedly contacted NB ACORN asking when someone would actually be coming and when the promised work would begin.

Before the beginning of September, I contacted them again and explicitly told them that I no longer wanted to be a member. I specifically instructed them not to withdraw any further money from my bank account. Despite that, money was subsequently taken from my account.

I am extremely disappointed—not simply because the promised assistance never materialized, but because I made it very clear that I wanted to cancel and did not authorize another payment.

My personal experience with NB ACORN did not match the expectations that were set for me when I signed up. I was promised substantial support and action, and I did not receive it.

I am still seeking the return of the money that was taken from me after I had requested cancellation.

Based on my experience, I would strongly encourage anyone considering becoming a member to make sure they understand exactly what assistance they will actually receive, when it will happen, and how membership payments and cancellation are handled.

I am extremely disappointed with how AAA Storage handled my belongings.
I was only four days past the date I was supposed to have everything removed when I contacted them. I was told there was nothing they could do about my belongings until Monday and that they would call me back that day. I did not owe any money on my storage unit.
Monday came and I never received a call. I called again Tuesday and left a message, but nobody got back to me. I called again Wednesday and finally reached someone. I was told that my belongings had already been disposed of.
What was especially upsetting was the way I was treated when I called. The person I spoke with was dismissive and, in my experience, seemed almost amused, smirking or laughing while telling me my  belongings were gone, and he hung up on me. I was actively trying to deal with the situation and had been told they would call me Monday. I was never given written notice that my belongings were going to be disposed of. I also never received a copy of my storage lease or agreement.I was actively trying to resolve the situation and had been told they would call me Monday. I was never given written notice that my belongings were going to be disposed of. I'm also concerned about whether the proper process was followed. Since I did not owe any money, I believe the company should explain what legal authority it relied on to dispose of my belongings and what notice, if any, was provided. Based on my experience, I highly recommend that people do not rent from this company. I found their handling of my situation extremely unprofessional.

WORST experience with Hoogveld Homes.

The way they treat tenants is incredibly disrespectful. When something needs to be fixed or there’s an issue with the home, suddenly nobody responds or you have to chase them repeatedly. But when THEY need something from you, they have no problem getting in touch.

We also had situations where they refused to handle things in what we believe was the proper legal way, and the whole process felt extremely sketchy and unprofessional.

What’s even more frustrating is that we’ve come across other tenants who have had very similar experiences with them. At some point, it stops feeling like a one-off bad experience and starts looking like a pattern.

I strongly recommend doing your research before renting from this company. Keep every email, text, and conversation in writing, take photos of everything, and know your rights as a tenant.

Based on our experience, I would NEVER rent from Hoogveld Homes again.

They do not properly honor the terms of their agreements. I would not recommend doing any financial transactions with this company. This experience cost us a lot of time and money. After searching on Facebook, I also found other people who had experienced similar issues.

I strongly recommend that anyone considering this firm think very carefully before paying them any money.

I clearly explained what I expected from the representation before retaining the firm. After they had my money, I found myself arguing with counsel late at night by email about those same expectations, with him disputing what I had originally communicated. Had his position been made clear before I paid, I would never have retained him.

I paid $2,000, yet the firm never went on the record as my counsel. After I terminated the relationship, the firm retained the entire $2,000 and treated a $6,000 trial fee as payable, while characterizing the remaining $4,300 as a “discretionary fee write-off.” I dispute this because the signed retainer specifically provides for a $1,000 file-opening and preliminary-advice fee upon premature termination.

I am now stuck trying to recover the additional $1,000 that I dispute they are entitled to keep. I have formally demanded its return, and at this point it appears I may have to take the matter through the Alberta Court of King’s Bench fee-review process just to try to get my money back.

The entire experience has caused me to lose trust in this firm. I would not retain them again and would strongly caution others to document exactly what they are being promised and understand every fee provision before handing over any money.

one_star_reviews.text:
If I could give this clinic 0stars, I would .
I had my first rhinoplasty in 2017 with Dr. Omar Fouda Neel. I originally had a long, bony nose, but after the surgery I was left with a very wide nose, a very bulbous tip, scars on the sides, and most importantly, a deep and very noticeable scar/indentation across the bridge of my nose that I still have today.

The result completely changed my life. It put me into a very deep depression for years. I struggled to work, go out, socialize, and even feel comfortable being around people. I eventually had to travel to Iran and have another surgery just to try to improve the shape of my nose. It helped somewhat, but I was still left with the deep scar on my bridge, the side scars, and the bulbous tip.

Dr. Fouda did try to fix the scar, but unfortunately it didn’t help. After that, instead of continuing to help me with the result of my surgery, he moved to Saudi Arabia and I was left to deal with everything on my own. He eventually blocked me on his social media platforms. After everything I had already gone through, being blocked by the surgeon who performed my surgery made me feel completely abandoned and dismissed. I was left with the scars, the results, and the emotional damage, while he simply moved on.

I also reached out to the Montreal clinic hoping they would help me, but I did not feel supported at all. I will never forget being told by the nurses, “Everything comes with a price,” and Dr. Fouda telling me, “I’m not a magician to fix it the way you want.” I wasn’t asking for magic or perfection. I was asking for help after a surgery that had such a huge impact on my life.

I am still dealing with the emotional effects of this experience today. I still struggle with depression, and I cannot afford the extremely high cost of another revision surgery to try to fix what happened.

This experience has affected me for years emotionally, financially, and personally. It is something I wish I had never gone through.

Based on my personal experience, I would never recommend this clinic or Dr. Fouda to anyone considering rhinoplasty. Please do your research very carefully before trusting someone with something as important as your face.

I’m very disappointed with this service. I paid $55 for a Bio Gel manicure and I’m not happy with the result.

First, I had an appointment and still had to wait around 45 minutes before being attended. I understand that delays can happen, but 45 minutes is a long time when you already booked an appointment.

The technician was also very rough with my hands and nails, especially when filing them. She was so rough that she even caused a small cut on my skin.

My nails were left uneven. Some are longer on one side, the shapes are different from nail to nail, and the filing is not uniform. Someone might say this happened because my nails were too short, but that is not the case. My nails were actually quite long before the service. I simply prefer my nails short, but I still expect them to be even, well shaped, and properly finished.

Another disappointing part was choosing the color. This salon has a large variety of color catalogs, and during my previous visits I was always shown all of them. Today, the color I wanted was not in the catalog she gave me. I say “catalog” because she gave me two, but they were actually the same one. She did not take the time to show me the full color selection, and it felt like a lack of effort and customer service. As a result, I had to choose a different color that was not what I originally wanted.

The application around the cuticles and sides is also not clean, and overall the service felt rushed and lacked attention to detail.

What makes me especially sad is that one bad service can affect the image of the whole salon. I have been coming here for several months, as you can probably see from my visit card, and until now I had always been happy with the final result. I understand that some technicians may be more experienced than others, but attitude and customer service make a big difference. Unfortunately, the attitude and the service I received today left a lot to be desired.

For $55, I expected a much better and more professional result. This experience was very disappointing and makes me question whether I would return.

one_star_reviews.text: I am writing this review to warn other women to protect their physical safety, their fertility, and their emotional well-being before coming here. When I first admitted to this clinic, it turned out I was already in the very early stages of a natural pregnancy. Despite my documented history of miscarriages, the clinic refused my explicit requests for further serial blood work and standard placement ultrasounds after just two initial blood tests. Instead of checking my rising numbers or confirming the pregnancy was safely inside my uterus, they brushed me off, told me "congratulations," and instructed me to just go book an OB appointment at 12 weeks. Because of this dangerous neglect, my ectopic pregnancy went completely undetected until it ruptured, resulting in severe physical and emotional trauma, emergency surgery, and the permanent loss of my fallopian tube. Because I was deeply unhappy with their work and their handling of my emergency, I decided to leave the clinic. However, they turned to deceptive, coercive tactics to prevent me from walking away. They falsely claimed that my turn for government-funded in vitro fertilization (IVF) was "locked" with their clinic, that I had "no chance" to go to another facility, and told me my only option was to switch to a different doctor within their own building. Fearing I had no other choice because of their lies, I stayed and went on to do an IVF cycle with them, where the mismanagement continued. They rushed my stimulation protocol and allowed my internal LH hormone to surge wildly to 58.25 mIU/L, which ruined my egg maturity. They then triggered me with a high-risk hCG shot despite my high follicle count, causing severe, painful ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) and fluid pooling. Out of 24 eggs, 10 were degenerated or empty, resulting in zero normal embryos. The clinic refused to take responsibility for their protocol mistakes, simply blaming my age and telling me my eggs were "low quality." Immediately after this first cycle of IVF failed with such terrible results, they tried to trap me further. To cover up their protocol mistakes and profit off their own failures, they suggested I do a second round with them, offering a "discounted" follow-up cycle for $9,000 instead of their standard rate. I successfully refused their high-pressure tactics, left, and moved to a new clinic under an expert doctor. With the exact same body and age, my new doctor locked down my LH, paced my cycle correctly, and safely retrieved 26 eggs, resulting in a 95% maturity rate and 90.5% beautifully fertilized embryos on Day 1 with zero bloating or pain. My eggs and my body were never the problem; this clinic's systematic neglect, dishonesty, financial manipulation, and generic care were. They endangered my life and cost me a fallopian tube. Please advocate for yourself and go elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
Whoever made the decision to add MoneyGram to this Post Office made a terrible decision. There is only one staff member working at the Post Office, and now that MoneyGram has been introduced, the line does not move.
I was there for over 40 minutes and had to renew my paid parking while waiting. There was only one customer ahead of me, but Leticia, the staff member working, took an incredibly long time assisting him. Meanwhile, everyone behind me had simple packages that should have taken only a couple of minutes to process.
To make matters worse, after nearly completing the first customer’s transaction, there weren’t enough certificates to give him his money. Leticia’s computer was put on hold while she tried calling a manager for help — who apparently wouldn’t even answer their phone.
Eventually, she was able to open the second computer to start processing the rest of us, but only after phoning another employee to use their login info. Why wasn’t another staff member sent to help when there was a long line of customers waiting?
I asked Leticia why there couldn’t be more staff available to help her. Her response was: “No, that’s okay. People are just particular.”
Excuse me? This response completely missed the point. This wasn’t about me worrying about her. Customers had been standing in line for over 40 minutes for basic postal transactions, and I had to pay additional parking because of the delay. That is not being “particular.” That is a legit customer service issue.
MoneyGram should never have been added to this location without ensuring adequate staffing and a system that doesn’t hold up everyone else in line. If MoneyGram is staying, more staff need to be available to handle these transactions.
This experience was frustrating, unnecessarily time-consuming, and completely unacceptable.

Huge thank you to Cristina in Cosmetics for helping me tape up a small parcel I was trying to ship, especially when I was in a rush!

I went to the Canada Post counter inside Shoppers with a prepaid parcel that simply needed to be taped closed. The woman at the counter told me they no longer provide tape and wouldn’t help close the box. I ship things frequently and have never encountered this before.

What should have taken a few seconds would have turned into such an unnecessary hassle—having to leave the counter, find tape in the store, buy an entire roll just to seal one small box etc..

Even if that’s the policy, it would have been so easy to help the customer this once and simply let me know for next time. The contrast in customer service really stood out: Cristina wasn’t even working at Canada Post, yet she immediately helped me out. Thank you, Cristina! I really appreciated it.🙏🏼

one_star_reviews.text:
During the CNE period, I visited the Starbucks location inside Hotel X Toronto. It happened to be my birthday, so my husband and I stopped by to redeem my Starbucks birthday reward before heading to the CNE.

The store was not particularly busy at the time, and I didn’t have to wait long. When it was my turn, I told the staff member that I would like to use my birthday reward. At first, they simply replied, “Okay,” but then remained silent without giving any further guidance or asking any questions. Unsure of what to do next, I waited for a moment. Then, the staff member asked in a somewhat irritated tone and attitude, essentially saying, “So, what are you going to order?” From that point on, I felt taken aback by why I was being treated this way.

My intention was to use my birthday reward for my drink and order my husband’s drink together, paying for his separately. However, even as I mentioned that I was ordering two drinks, the staff member’s response felt rather blunt. The atmosphere felt so awkward that I wondered if they thought I was trying to get two free drinks with one reward, so I explained that I would pay for the second drink separately.

The payment process was also confusing and frustrating due to poor communication. I showed my Starbucks app to redeem the birthday reward, but I wanted to pay for my husband’s drink with our joint credit card. However, the staff member never asked or explained how the payment would be processed, and after taking the order, they said nothing further, so I was waiting for instructions. When I mentioned that I wanted to pay by credit card, they simply said, “Oh...” and mentioned that it had already been processed, without any further explanation or attempt to resolve the issue. Not wanting to prolong the interaction, I just said it was fine and left.

Usually, when I visit Starbucks to use a birthday reward, staff members warmly say “Happy Birthday” or smoothly guide the ordering process. This time, however, I was met with short responses and an overall cold, irritated attitude, which was very disappointing. Overall, I felt unwelcome. I believe this situation wouldn't have been an issue at all if there had been just a little more kindness and smooth communication.

Because of these experiences, I left the store feeling upset. It was especially disappointing because I had stopped by on my birthday morning, hoping to start a fun day with my husband before going to the CNE.

Extremely disappointing and unprofessional management at the Woodstock location.
I have had an extremely frustrating experience with this clinic. My appointments were cancelled twice in less than two weeks, both times after I had already arrived at the clinic. I was not contacted in advance to inform me of the cancellations. When I questioned this, I was told that the clinic had called but that no one answered. I strongly dispute this, as I received no calls or messages notifying me of the changes.
What was even more disappointing was the way my complaint was handled. Instead of acknowledging the inconvenience and taking responsibility, the staff responded rudely and made it seem as though the situation was somehow the client's fault. This is completely unacceptable.
The summer vacation is almost over, yet the clinic has still not completed my family's treatment. Only my older son has received treatment, while the rest of my family is still waiting for the clinic to begin providing the services we need. The delays and lack of communication have been extremely frustrating.
What concerns me most is that even when feedback is provided to management, there appears to be little willingness to listen or address the client's concerns. Instead, responsibility is shifted back onto the client rather than addressing the clinic's own communication and scheduling failures.
A healthcare clinic should value its clients' time, communicate clearly, and take responsibility when mistakes occur. Unfortunately, my experience at the Woodstock location has been the complete opposite. I would strongly recommend that management take these concerns seriously and make significant improvements to their scheduling, communication, and customer service.

one_star_reviews.text: My 94 year old Mother died in palliative “care” six days after being admitted to the  fifth floor of this hospital in April of 2023. The staff did not put any nutrients in her IV, it only held a lethal cocktail of drugs that, let’s face it, hastened her demise . No my beautiful Mother did not ask for MAID but it appears to have occurred anyway. She was 100% with it and sharp as a tack when admitted . Yes she was dying slowly after four years of lung cancer. (Non smoker) Some of the fifth floor palliative care nurses are somewhat lazy and sit around yapping amongst themselves. Having said that we did meet some kind, professional nurses but I question how long they will stay in that underperforming environment. The middle aged bitter, curt and insensitive nurse with short blond hair might serve the world  better in a job where she doesn’t deal with people let alone those virtually helpless individuals who are most deserving of the utmost dignity and respect in their vulnerable and final days. I met three brothers up there who told  me their Father had not been fed in almost a week. Horrified, I spoke with nurses and two Drs who explained briefly something about nourishment would flood their organs and cause more pain. Well I wish we knew this was  going to take place before agreeing and encouraging her to go back to the hospital for care. Apparently I was wrong thinking hospital care meant Drs and staff doing everything possible to keep her alive. I googled and read about sponge lollipops so asked a nurse for some and I gave my poor dehydrated Mother some water on the sponge as she kept stressing how thirsty she was. But the next day when I visited Mum the sponges were put away out of her sight and reach. I found them in a drawer. Sadly by then Mum was in a drug induced coma and died later that day. I’m mad, sad and frightened for the state of health “care” with socialized medicine in Canada. The stuff of nightmares and an experience that will haunt me forever!  My heart goes out to everyone who has suffered and was treated in a less than transparent, respectful and dignified manner while in the hospital. 100% completely unnecessary and unacceptable. Fix it please and thank you.

I am very disappointed with the care I received from my primary midwife, Alice. The further along my pregnancy progressed, the less involved she seemed, especially after I learned my baby was breech and that I would be delivering in the hospital. She missed a postpartum phone appointment without apologizing, called me back two weeks later as if nothing had happened, and completely ignored me after telling me to come to the birthing center for my blood test and Pap test.

The most serious failing was in the scheduling of my cesarean section. She confirmed she had booked the date at the hospital and gave me the doctor's name. Less than a week before the scheduled date, having received no confirmation, I called the hospital: nothing had been scheduled for me. This medical negligence forced me to organize everything at the last minute, an unacceptable source of stress for a breech pregnancy.

Imposing such a level of stress on a pregnant woman, whose situation was already precarious due to a breech baby, demonstrates a blatant lack of commitment on the part of this professional. Furthermore, the affiliated hospital (Maisonneuve-Rosemont) made this experience traumatic due to the disrespectful and racist attitude of its staff.

There's nothing wrong with the structure of the birthing center itself, but the quality of the experience unfortunately depends entirely on the midwife you receive.

one_star_reviews.text:
We were at Main Through Church Antiques shopping on Friday and bought several items from a booth that was advertised at 70% off. We left our items at the front desk while we continued shopping. When we went to pay, the total had already been calculated for us, so we paid without seeing an itemized bill.
When we got home, we realized that the amount we paid did not match what we had purchased. Unfortunately, all of the price tags had been removed, so we couldn’t even go back and verify the individual prices. Based on what we remembered, it appeared that we had been overcharged significantly, and the 70% discount did not seem to have been applied as advertised.
I was extremely disappointed because I thought we had gotten some great deals, only to realize afterward that we had likely paid close to full price.
My advice to anyone shopping here: make sure you get an itemized bill before paying, and if a booth is offering a percentage discount, double-check that the discount has actually been taken off.
This experience really took the enjoyment out of what should have been a fun day of antique shopping. Very disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
I never write reviews, but after our experience with A1 Granite, I feel it’s important to share what happened.
Unfortunately, our experience was extremely unprofessional and frustrating. I strongly recommend paying close attention to the reviews before choosing this company.

We were quoted different prices at different points, with significant discrepancies in the pricing.

We paid a deposit, only to have the slab we selected damaged/broken. A1 Granite has denied responsibility for the damage, but we have pictures that tell a very different story.

What made the situation even more frustrating was that the selection available to us was very limited. We were unable to find another option that worked with our color scheme, leaving us with very few alternatives. Despite the circumstances, we were still charged a restocking fee for the slab that was broken.

Rather than taking accountability and working with us to resolve the situation, we felt that the blame was placed back on us as the customers.

The biggest disappointment wasn’t simply the additional $500—it was the lack of customer service and accountability throughout the entire experience.

There are many other reputable companies and great options available. Based on our experience, I would strongly recommend considering other companies before doing business with A1 Granite.

We completed two kitchen projects with this company. The installation was handled through the Saskatoon office, while most communication was through the Calgary office so we will be leaving this review in both places appropriately.

Both kitchens were incorrectly templated and measured. They also failed to show up with even the proper materials on installation day to complete. The resulting countertops were unusable for our project and quite literally could not have even be installed that day due to not fitting or covering required gaps in cabinets and an entire sit up overhang was completely missed. As I write this review, the countertops from both kitchens are fully wasted material and are still sitting on the floor months later because they could not be used. We ultimately had to hire another contractor to redo the entire project(s).

Throughout the process, the company blamed us for issues that that arose from their templating and measurement errors such as referencing our rough numbers used to get preliminary quotes (as they are not local and require this to even get started). Even when mistakes were identified, we were unable to obtain an acceptable resolution.

Our concerns were dismissed, conversations were often confrontational, and the company refused to take responsibility for the problems and blamed us for countertops being the wrong size even though their own contract verbiage and common industry practice of required templating disproves this. The only solution offered was for us to pay additional money to have their own mistakes corrected.

As a result, we have incurred thousands of dollars in additional costs and are currently pursuing litigation to recover our losses.

Based on our experience with two separate kitchens, I would strongly recommend looking elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
I go to this church because it’s beautiful, and I can still find God here, but navigating the services at the church has been a nightmare.
There is no place for someone who is trying to understand the faith and learn the many intricate rules and traditions of Orthodoxy. There is, however, a lot of judgment and shame from the priests for not already knowing, hence why this is also anonymous.
I was born in Ethiopia and know some things. However, having grown up here, I’ve found that there are a lot of intricate rules to navigate.
The priests like to preach about making time for confession. However, trying to actually find a priest to confess to took me nearly three years.
I gave up completely on trying to get a membership. The first time I tried, about three years ago, they weren’t accepting memberships. The second time, I filled out the form and was told I needed to get a priest to witness and sign it as my confession father. The last time, I got a priest to sign it, and the lady at the desk accused me of forging his signature. I cried that day and gave up on becoming a member, which was a prerequisite for getting into a WhatsApp group where I could receive information about events, etc.
That lady is so disrespectful and rude that I never want to deal with her again. She also seems to be in charge of the books. I gave a $200 donation, for which I never received a donation receipt because the process of getting one is so convoluted. Rather than issuing one when the donation is made, they give you a useless receipt and ask you to come back months later, sign up once again, and follow up multiple times. I now give my donations to another church that issues its receipts right away.
So far, I’ve been insulted, shamed, and belittled. I now have a priest from this church after observing each one over the last three years, and I’m grateful for him.
But overall, as a young adult who grew up in Canada and is trying to grow in my faith, this church has been a disappointment. I’ve had more luck getting guidance and support from churches in Toronto and the U.S. than I have here.

one_star_reviews.text:
Would leave zero stars if I could. Moved with this company 1.5 years ago and was too exhausted and busy to leave a review at the time, but heard about another friend’s bad experience with them and after seeing some similar reviews, I decided to share ours. We were quoted 5 hours to move a few blocks away, and they took 13 hours. I can see taking a hour or two extra, but not over DOUBLE the amount of time we were quoted based on the distance and items we own. They arrived late, and things took so long that my husband, myself, both of my parents, and my brother in law helped them in the last few hours because it was getting so late. One of the guys had just started that day and was walking at such a slow pace between loads that the other mover actually told me that I was more efficient than his partner.

We had everything packed in boxes ahead of time and had even moved a bunch of them over ahead of time. We didn’t even own a couch or chairs. They also insisted on completely taking apart our 2 ikea wardrobes, which ate up a bunch of time. For reference, we had a third wardrobe that someone picked up fully intact via Facebook marketplace—they don’t need to be taken apart to move. They also lost part of our bed, so we had to duct tape it together until we could replace it.

When they finally arrived at our new building about 7 hours in and parked in the loading zone, they asked for a break to get a sandwich across the street. We were fine with them taking a break, but they attempted to include that time in the overall charge for the move after already being far over the quoted time. They then asked me to stand in the busy 4-lane street and direct traffic around the truck while they unloaded. After I refused, they pulled out some orange cones and put them around the truck while they unloaded. Why are you asking your clients to stand in the street if you have the equipment? Completely unprofessional and unsafe, and deliberately wasted our time and money.

one_star_reviews.text:
My family and I travelled with Air France in July and August 2026, with bookings totalling more than €8,500. This review is therefore based on a genuine, personal, and documented customer experience.

On July 20, our three minor children travelled to France, including two using the Kids Solo service. Following flight AF375 from Vancouver to Paris, they had to wait nearly eight hours at Paris-CDG before reaching their final destination, with late and inadequate information. At Vancouver Airport, Air France also required us to pay an additional CAD 800 for Kids Solo.

On August 22, despite arrangements made several months in advance through Saphir, staff attempted to move my wife, who has a severe disability, from Business Class to Economy. Her Business Class seat was restored only after an extremely distressing confrontation in front of our children.

I subsequently followed up personally on several claims with Air France. The incidents were divided among different files and representatives. Some claims were closed without a complete written explanation, documents already provided were requested again, and important questions remained unanswered. Despite our repeated requests, no senior representative has coordinated our family’s overall case.

This series of serious incidents, followed by the absence of a coordinated and meaningful response, explains my one-star rating.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Quality for the Price

Absolutely awful quality for the price.

We purchased new bedding from Hush with a total cost of over $600, specifically because we wanted to support a Canadian company and invest in what we expected to be higher-end, quality bedding.

Unfortunately, the quality has been incredibly disappointing. We just reached the two-year mark this past July, and multiple pieces are already falling apart. The comforter is ripping at the seams in multiple places, while the duvet cover initially developed loose threads that have now progressed to multiple areas coming apart as well.

We take extremely good care of our linens and have followed the manufacturer’s washing and care instructions. For bedding at this price point, I find this level of deterioration after less than two years completely unacceptable.

What makes this even more disappointing is that we have purchased both higher- and lower-priced bedding from companies such as Pottery Barn and IKEA and have never experienced this kind of premature deterioration with their linens.

I contacted Hush to give them an opportunity to address the issue. Despite spending over $600 on their products, the only resolution they were willing to offer was 30% off a future purchase. Why would I spend more money on a product that has already failed prematurely?

A discount on another purchase is not an appropriate resolution when the original products have not held up to reasonable expectations of quality and durability.

Unfortunately, based on both the product quality and the customer service response, I will not be purchasing from Hush again and cannot recommend them to others. If you are considering spending a significant amount of money on their bedding, I would strongly encourage you to look elsewhere.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would avoid this place.

The board is extremely quick to issue warnings—or fines—when they see something they believe violates the condo rules. However, when you bring an issue to their attention, they take forever to respond, and sometimes you don’t hear back at all.

For example, I received a warning (luckily not a fine) for having a trash bin on my balcony. I understand that there are rules to follow, but it felt invasive knowing that board members were apparently monitoring individual units closely enough to catch something like this.

Meanwhile, my partner and I dealt with a neighbour smoking weed several times a day throughout the summer. The smell would constantly enter our unit, to the point where we had to keep our windows closed because we could never predict when he would smoke. I contacted property management several times hoping they would address the issue, but very little was done.

This turned into an entire summer of back-and-forth emails, with responses sometimes taking around two weeks. We repeatedly had to follow up on our case, only to receive the same automated-sounding responses. Eventually, we realized that no one was actually going to resolve the issue, so we tried to take matters into our own hands—but unsurprisingly, the situation did not improve.

We are now having to move out early because the smoking is still happening upstairs, and we recently brought a newborn home. We obviously don’t want to take any unnecessary risks with second-hand smoke. Having to move unexpectedly is a huge inconvenience and an expense that could have potentially been avoided if our concerns had been taken seriously in the first place.

Overall, my experience has been that the management company and/or board seems far more concerned with maintaining the appearance and enforcing the rules of the building than with addressing the actual concerns and wellbeing of the people living there.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend this place.

one_star_reviews.text:
Steve provided good service when selling my wife a Husqvarna e-bike in the summer of 2026. Unfortunately, what followed was a disappointing experience with the service department at the North Vancouver shop.

During the bike’s first “free” service, they found that the cassette was loose. It was unclear whether this was an issue that existed when the bike left the shop. They also recommended replacing the chain, which had only 1,500 km on it, without clearly explaining the options or the cost beforehand.

When I went to pick up the bike, I was presented with a $130 bill for the chain. I refused to pay the charge and asked for the old chain back, but they did not provide it. I walked out of the door with no chain.

In my opinion, any repair service should be discussed with the customer first, with clear options and a quote before the work is carried out. A $130 charge for a bicycle chain—regardless of whether it is marketed as an “e-bike” chain—seems excessive. There are several nearby bike shops that offer more transparent advice and reasonable prices. Sports Junkies, in particular, has been great in my experience so far: honest advice and decent prices.

Unfortunately, this experience has made it difficult for me to trust the work being done at this shop. I would recommend getting a second opinion and a quote elsewhere before authorizing any repairs.

Absolutely unacceptable delivery service.

Metro Supply Chain has failed to deliver my package TWICE. Both attempts were around 9 PM. How is this considered a delivery attempt? Calling once from a blocked number at 9 PM and then leaving is not a reasonable attempt to deliver a package.

I have now contacted Metro by email and expect my package to be delivered tomorrow, during reasonable hours, and left at my apartment door as requested.

This is by far one of the worst delivery experiences I have had. Metro needs to fix both its delivery procedures and its complete lack of accessible customer service.

They advised that they made two attempts to make the delivery, two days in a row, and that these attempts were not successful.  They never contacted me at the provided number to advise that there was an issue.

Now this is important:  I sent the package to my workplace.  My workplace is open 24/7 x 365.  Nobody every attempted to make this delivery.  If they had, it would have been completed.

I was subsequently emailed twice with links from the provider, advising that there were attempts to deliver.  The emails had links for me to click to resolve the issue.  I clicked the links.  They were both dead.

I then attempted to find contact information for the carrier.  They have a web form which I filled out and they didn't bother replying to.  As far as I can tell, there is no contact number on their website whatsoever.

If you are a vendor, please understand that this logistics company is abosolute trash. Worst I have ever dealt with.  If you use Metro to fullfull your clients needs, you clients are going to have many problems.

Instead, when we arrived, we were told to go home and wait for a phone call to tell us how to proceed. That is absolutely not what we needed. We needed to see a doctor ASAP.

Rather than go home and wait for a call (?), we had to sit for four hours at Eagle Ridge just to get an X‑ray. He now has a suspected serious rotator cuff injury, and the hospital will be contacting him with an ultrasound time tomorrow. He’ll be off work for at least a month, will require physio, and is currently on a strong dose of Tylenol 3’s for the pain.

What’s the point of an “urgent primary care” center if it can’t provide care when it’s actually needed? Completely ineffective setup.

If you need URGENT care I would NOT recommend.  It appears to be an Urgent and Primary Care Centre in name only.

I've been banking at this TD branch for over ten years, and for most of that time the staff have been consistently helpful and professional — it's the main reason I've stayed loyal to this location.

However, my last two visits were disappointing. A young man was training a new employee, which I have no issue with — training is a normal part of running a branch. My concern is how he conducted himself while doing it. The training visibly took priority over the transaction, so things took much longer than usual. When I needed to add a personal pay option to my company account — something I'm familiar with from past experience, as the setup can be a bit particular — I tried to explain how it worked. He brushed off what I was saying, didn't engage with it at all, and instead of addressing my concern just said "you're good to go" and moved on.

That kind of dismissive attitude toward a long-time customer isn't acceptable, especially from someone currently training other staff. I'd hope the branch looks into how customer concerns are being handled during onboarding, because it doesn't reflect the standard I've come to expect here over the past decade.

one_star_reviews.text:
🚨 🚨 1,000,000% DO NOT RECOMMEND — BUYER BEWARE! 🚨

My experience with SpaBerry and its customer service was absolutely unacceptable.

Both Jeff Knight (President) and Kevin Smith (Senior Vice President of Operations) were, in my experience, extremely rude, dismissive, and completely lacking in professionalism.
They certainly seem to have mastered the “gift of gab”, saying all the right things when it suits them, making promises and providing assurances, but when it came time to actually stand behind those words and provide clear, honest answers, the experience was an entirely different story.

I ordered a SpaBerry SB5 in August 2026. A few weeks after the order, I had some legitimate questions regarding the electrical requirements and specifications for the unit, as I was beginning preparing for the installation and arrival of the tub. What followed was extremely concerning.

After spending money on a custom concrete pad, specifically sized for the tub that I ordered, I was looking for some specific technical information about the electrical requirements, from SpaBerry. Instead, I encountered what I felt was a surprising lack of knowledge, vague answers, and very little in the way of concrete technical information.

Once it became apparent that I understood the electrical side of the installation and was asking questions that required specific answers, communication essentially stopped.

My calls and emails went unanswered. I followed their own protocol on their website for a dispute and quickly learned that the dispute goes right back to the only two people that appear to be in the company… the ones that I had the original dispute with…

Then, rather than addressing my questions or providing the technical documentation I had requested, my order was cancelled.

The explanation I received was essentially that “a SpaBerry tub isn’t right for you.” And they essentially stiffed me with all the costs for the significant preparations I made before the tub’s arrival. When questioned, their answer was simply “We aren’t going to cover any of that”.

That experience left me with some very serious questions:

If a company is selling a product that requires electrical installation, customers should be able to obtain clear, accurate and verifiable information regarding the electrical specifications and applicable certifications when purchasing the product.

I have not been provided with satisfactory answers to my questions, and that raises concerns for me about whether SpaBerry units have the appropriate electrical approvals / certifications for their intended installation.

And when a company responds to legitimate technical questions by effectively telling the customer, “this product isn't right for you,” rather than answering those questions, and ignoring the costs and efforts put in by customers prior to the tub arriving, only to cancel for no reason or without any notice, well, that's a major red flag 🚩 in my books.

For reference, Canadian electrical safety authorities emphasize that electrical products must have appropriate recognized approvals / certifications & markings before being used or sold in applicable jurisdictions.

My recommendation - DO YOUR HOMEWORK!!

Ask questions. Ask for the actual certifications / approval documentation. Get the electrical specifications in writing and the nameplate information. And DON’T simply just take someone's word for it.

Based on my personal experiences, I strongly do not recommend SpaBerry. Not even remotely.

BUYER BEWARE. ⚠️
